Jon —

Appreciate the questionnaire, and thanks for flagging these items. I've looped in Laura (legal) and Karthik (infra/ops) so we can give concrete language and an operations plan.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Pen-test notice: Redwood typically requests a 10-business-day notice. We can do 14 calendar days as a concession; will confirm with infra on whether ephemeral staging creds and exportable sample sets are feasible under that window.
- SOC 2: we can provide the most recent Type II report; for change evidence, we typically provide a change log extract for the last 90 days.
- Inspection rights: Redwood prefers bounded inspection (pre-scheduled, scoped, and with agreed sample sets). We'll propose tightened language that includes scope limits and an ops hit list.

I'll attach a redline of the security exhibit with suggested swap-ins and an operational appendix for evidence delivery. Can we do a 30-minute workshop Friday 6/11 or Monday 6/14 to walk through specifics?

Jon / Tessa —

Thanks for the packet, Jon. I reviewed the questionnaire and drafted a few concrete edits into the security exhibit (high level here):

1) Audit/inspection rights — redline to "bounded inspection" only: scheduled, limited to agreed sample sets, no live production interruption, third-party counsel allowed if cleared in advance. We will not accept broad "unrestricted access" language.

2) Pen-testing — required to provide scope and test plan 10 business days prior; Redwood will provide ephemeral staging credentials for a single test window; results delivery: vendor provides an executive summary and redact PII before sharing. Evidence handoff will be through an agreed secure folder.

3) SOC 2 — Redwood will deliver the most recent Type II report under an NDA and provide a change-log extract for the last 90 days. We will not provide raw control evidence beyond that extract; instead we can schedule a focused evidence review call for items that need deeper inspection.

Operational asks for your team (Jon): please confirm the proposed sample set size (we suggest no greater than 1% of production user records or up to 500 items, whichever is smaller) and whether your counsel needs privileged forensic access.

I attached tracked changes. If ClearLake agrees to bounded inspection + ephemeral creds + a secure evidence folder, we can sign off on the exhibit and move the order form to DocuSign.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
